title: DigitalOcean Launches Learning and Data Services to Enable Self-Improving AI Agents
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/digitalocean-self-improving-ai/en/headerimage/digitalocean-managed-agents-1793035926117.jpeg"/><p>DigitalOcean has announced the public preview of Learning Services and Agent Data Services, enabling developers to build, evaluate, and continuously improve AI agents within a unified, AI-native, cloud platform.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Production AI and Engineering Team Design: InfoQ’s November Certification Cohorts
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/online-cohorts-nov-certification/en/headerimage/InfoQ-Nov-Cohorts-v3-1793013188536.jpg"/><p>A preview of three November InfoQ online certification cohorts covering production AI systems, retrieval and agent design, engineering team flow, AI roles, and measurement, facilitated by Adi Polak, Lan Chu, and Olimpiu Pop.</p> <i>By Artenisa Chatziou</i>

title: Java News Roundup: JDK 28 Schedule, Oracle CPUs, eMudhra Certs, Apache POI, WildFly, Azul, BellSoft
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/java-news-roundup-oct19-2026/en/headerimage/java-news-roundup-image-1793025199136.jpg"/><p>This week's Java roundup for October 19th, 2026, features news highlighting: the proposed release schedule for JDK 28; the eMudhra Intermediate CA certificates breach; the October 2026 Critical Patch Update; Azul and BellSoft CPUs; GA releases of WildFly 42 and Apache POI 6.0; the beta release of Open Liberty 26.0.0.11; and maintenance releases of Micronaut and JobRunr.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

title: Readyon Builds Four Layer Tenant Isolation for Multi Tenant Amazon EKS
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>ReadyOn has detailed a four-layer tenant isolation architecture for its Harmony platform on Amazon EKS. The design combines Kubernetes namespaces, dedicated Karpenter node pools, VPC security groups, and per-tenant Aurora databases, with controls evaluated against a 10-stage multi-tenant threat model focused on cross-tenant access and lateral movement.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Article: The Evolution of Agentic Harnesses: From Chains to Graph to Code
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/agentic-ai-architecture-harness-evolution/en/headerimage/agentic-ai-architecture-harness-evolution-header-1792744961862.jpg"/><p>Agentic LLM systems have moved from linear prompt chains to graph-based workflows and, more recently, code-executing harnesses. Chains are simple but fragile, graphs add branching, retries, and validation, and code harnesses verify outputs through execution. The article advises validating model outputs and choosing the least complex design that meets reliability, speed, and cost needs.</p> <i>By Karthik Ramgopal</i>

title: Cloudflare’s Auto Router Rates Each Request for Stakes, from the Most Recent Turns
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-auto-router/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792492628413.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has released Auto Router in public beta through AI Gateway, picking a model per request from a classifier that scores complexity, ambiguity, stakes and context dependence. Cloudflare’s own benchmark puts it ten points below Claude Opus 5.5 on success rate at a third of the cost, and practitioners have questioned how stakes survive a long agent session.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: MCP C# SDK 2.0 Makes HTTP Stateless by Default and Adds Multi Round-Trip Requests
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/MCP-CSharp-SDK-Stateless/en/headerimage/header-1792707557585.jpg"/><p>Microsoft announced version 2.0 of the official MCP C# SDK, which implements the 2026-07-28 revision of the Model Context Protocol with stateless HTTP servers by default, standardised routing headers and Multi Round-Trip Requests. Releases 2.1 to 2.3 have since added hybrid session serving, a subscriptions/listen handler and a series of discovery, OAuth and shutdown fixes.</p> <i>By Edin Kapić</i>

title: PHP Patches Two Critical RCE Flaws That Were Already Under Attack
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/php-critical-rce-patches/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792866020447.jpg"/><p>PHP released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 to fix two critical vulnerabilities allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Amazon recorded an exploitation attempt four days before the patches shipped, and operators spent the day working out whether they ran PHP, where to get the package, and how to tell it had landed.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: PyTorch Conference 2026: Google and Meta Open-Source TorchTPU for Native PyTorch on TPUs
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/google-meta-torchtpu/en/headerimage/torchtpu-header-1792934272172.jpg"/><p>Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Google's TPUs, at PyTorch Conference North America 2026, and Meta said it plans to move larger LLM workloads onto TPUs with it. AWS released TorchNeuron for Trainium the same week, while developers questioned TPU availability and where vendor lock-in now sits.</p> <i>By Andrew Hoblitzell</i>

title: Google ML Drift Accelerates On-Device AI Inference Across Diverse GPUs
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/google-ml-drift/en/headerimage/gemini-agentic-vision-1792946554031.jpg"/><p>Google has released ML Drift, an open-source, cross-platform GPU compute engine designed for on-device AI and machine learning inference. Licensed under Apache 2.0, it abstracts the complexities of different GPU hardware and low-level APIs, supporting OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal, and WebGPU.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: PingCAP Breach Exposes Customer Records and Source Code
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/pingcap-cloud-data-breach/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792787545089.jpg"/><p>PingCAP recently confirmed unauthorized access to its internal systems and the theft of source code and customer-related data. The attacker, cyber extortion group FulcrumSec, claimed to have stolen 10.6 TB of data, including TiDB Cloud control-plane records, customer SQL statements, API keys, connection logs, billing information, internal documents, and 413 private source-code repositories.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Google Optimizes Agent Development Kit's 200K-line Python Codebase Overnight with Gemini 4 Argon
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/google-argon-optimizes-adk/en/headerimage/functiongemma-1792855681633.jpeg"/><p>Google explained how an 11-hour unattended run of Gemini 4 Argon produced two accepted optimizations for Google Agent Development Kit's codebase, reducing in-memory session-preparation overhead by about 40% in long sessions and cold package import time by 21%.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Google’s Data Agent Kit Hits GA, Splitting Agent Guardrails Between Skills and IAM
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Google has made Data Agent Kit generally available, a free set of MCP tools and 37 open-source skills that connect coding agents to more than fifteen Google Data Cloud services. Two kinds of guardrail ship with it, and practitioners need to tell them apart: one is a skill asking the agent to stop, the other an IAM deny policy that refuses the call.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Cloudflare Reclaims 100 TB of RAM by Optimizing Consistent Hashing
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-hashing-optimization/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790410589563.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare recently documented how it reduced the memory footprint of its internal load-balancing service by more than 100 TB by optimizing the Rust implementation of consistent hashing in pingora-ketama. The changes compacted hash-ring entries and used statistical analysis of hash distribution and collision rates to reduce the number of hashes per backend by about 90%.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: CSIRO Uses Serverless Architecture to Query 100x More Genomic Variants on AWS
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>CSIRO has developed Serverless Beacon, a serverless architecture for querying genomic variants without copying VCF files into a central database. The system combines Amazon S3, Lambda, Athena and DynamoDB, using metadata indexes and HTTP byte range requests to query compressed genomic regions. Tests reported 1.52 second average latency for 10,000 base pair queries.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>
